question: When we write instructions for an AI agent, are we teaching it facts or showing it the steps?
reflection: Good habits written as clear steps help machines and people alike, and the practice of writing them makes our own work clearer.

sources.subject: AI agent skills: Why they succeed and what causes them to crash

one_line: A large study suggests agent skills work best as step-by-step checklists, not as stores of knowledge.

top_stories.title: Agent skills work as checklists, not lessons
top_stories.what: Researchers reviewed more than 8,000 agent trials and found that skills mostly help by keeping the agent on a steady sequence of steps, rarely by adding new facts.
top_stories.why: This matches what behavioural science knows about checklists in surgery and aviation, and gives a clear way to write agent guidance.

top_stories.title: Unlabelled past runs make agents worse
top_stories.what: When skills were built from past attempts without marking which ones succeeded, success reportedly fell from about 75% to 40%.
top_stories.why: Learning from experience only works when outcomes are recorded honestly, for machines as for teams.

top_stories.title: Too many skills confuse the agent
top_stories.what: As the skill library grew from 5 to 100, agents picked the exact right skill far less often, though related skills still helped them finish.
top_stories.why: Sorting guidance into clear groups first, then using strict triggers, keeps large libraries usable.

idea.title: Runbooks for research agents
idea.pitch: Turn the team's best research procedures, such as survey cleaning or interview coding, into short step lists that agents and new staff can both follow.
idea.first_step: Pick one routine task and write it as no more than ten numbered steps.

idea_kids.title: My step-by-step recipe card
idea_kids.pitch: Children write a picture recipe for a simple task, like making a sandwich, then a partner follows it exactly to see which steps were missing.
idea_kids.first_step: Print a blank recipe card with six numbered boxes for drawings.
